Hello everyone. I'd like to present to you for review a proof the maximum Laplacian ratio of a tree. This work gives a complete answer to the open question Brualdi and Goldwasser posed in 1984, fully kernel-checked in Lean:

Resolved: For every n ≥ 4, the tree on n vertices maximizing the Laplacian ratio per L(T) / ∏ deg(v) is an explicit spider of cherry arms, and the maximum grows exactly like ((621/64)^(1/11))^n. The maximizer is unique up to isomorphism for every n ≥ 4 except n = 21, where exactly T(3,3,3) and S(21,10) are maximal.

https://zenodo.org/records/23269615
https://drmurphyisin.github.io/brualdi-goldwasser/

This work is fully Kernel-checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib, using only the standard axioms. The statement of the maximum and a maximizer is re-checked by a second, independently implemented kernel (nanoda, via the Lean FRO's Comparator).
